messages:
Ravi Desai: Quick post-RFC sync: we need a pragmatic path from LeaseTokens -> minimal API that operators can run without major frag regressions. I'm proposing: reserve(id, mode=\"ephemeral\"|\"sticky\", ttl_ms=60000) + release(id). Default ephemeral, sticky behind a tenant quota and FF.

Emilia Novak: Sounds workable. Two operator asks: 1) clear preemption signal in eviction-notify, 2) metric to correlate reservations with fragmentation.

Connor Blake: Implemented a simulator that replays mixed tenant traces and exercised a prototype reserve API. Quick results:
```
trace: mixed-chat + embeddings (rps 800)
baseline (lease token): p95=48ms, fragmentation_index=0.32, cost/op=1.00
reserve-ephemeral default: p95=52ms, fragmentation_index=0.36, cost/op=0.85
reserve-with-coalesce: p95=50ms, fragmentation_index=0.33, cost/op=0.87
```
Coalesce pass (incremental, rate-limited) recovers most frag impact. Without full compaction tails go up slightly.

Ravi Desai: Good numbers. We can't do stop-the-world compaction. What's coalesce overhead at host scale?

Connor Blake: Incremental coalesce uses an async worker scanning free runs and merging neighbors. On test host (A100, 512GB) a constrained pass takes ~100ms and can be throttled; it doesn't block inference. Full compaction is seconds and we should avoid it unless host idle.

Emilia Novak: On signals: eviction-notify should have fields {key, reason: \"preempted\"|\"evicted\", suggested_backoff_ms, timestamp}. Also add telemetry: tenant_reserve_count, tenant_frag_index, reserve_preemptions/sec. Alert rule suggestion: tenant_frag_index>0.6 && reserve_preemptions>2/s.

Connor Blake: Also saw pathological case: small tenants issuing many short TTL sticky reservations can starve co-tenants. We added per-tenant reserve_budget (token-bucket) and a global reserve_admission limiter to prevent ratholes; simulator shows stability with budget=10 credits/min.

Ravi Desai: Rollout plan: land reserve API behind FF (memory.reserve.simple=false). Enable ephemeral reserves first (sticky disabled). Enable incremental coalesce in background on canary fleet. Canary traffic: 1% -> 10% -> 50% gates: p95, fragmentation_index, reserve_preemptions. Owners: Connor (sim and coalesce), Emilia (telemetry + alerts), Ravi (rollout).

infra-bot: feature-flag memory.reserve.simple created. Canary scheduled: group=canary-omega start=Fri 01:00 UTC. Dashboards: /d/memory/reserve-simple (owner: @Emilia).

Emilia Novak: I'll add a tenant-level frag heatmap API and a new metric frag_run_length_avg to surface micro-frag. Also adding a suggestion in SDK docs: use reserve only for heavy-weight hot KV, avoid reserving per-request. Provide sample code: reserve(prefix_key, ttl_ms=120000) and subscribe to eviction webhook to rewarm.

Connor Blake: Action items: I'll run extended sims with spike scenarios (all tenants pin) and tune token-bucket defaults. If we see poor fairness we'll add proportional demotion by tenant commit size.

Ravi Desai: Keep sticky off for initial run. If sims show controlled frag we can propose sticky behind tenant quota and manual opt-in. Also add an experimental "idle-compaction" that only triggers when host utilization < 20% for > 5m. That gives us a path to recover long-term fragmentation without impacting SLOs.

Emilia Novak: Agreed. I'll wire alerts and a dashboard that overlays reserve_count, frag_index, p95 and preemptions so ops can triage quickly.

Connor Blake: Will post sim links and datasets here when done (using Q4_replay + tracegen heavy_tail).

Ravi Desai: Great. Please ping when sim results are up and I'll schedule a 30m follow-up if needed. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary created (id: canary-2026-08-12-09).
